End-to-End Pipeline: Muscle signal -> amplification -> filtering -> microcontroller -> actuation
Filtering: Used to remove high-frequency noise and stabilize the EMG signal
PCB Fabrication: Manually fabricated using a copper-clad board
Output Control: Servo motor actuation based on muscle activity
Testing Method: Live EMG signal acquisition from arm muscles
Testing Result: Successful control of a servo motor using muscle signals
Validation: Noise reduction effective for basic control
Core Features: Noise filtering using a low-pass filter
Limitations: No notch filter for 50/60Hz noise removal
No instrumentation amplifier, resulting in lower precision
No advanced signal processing such as RMS or envelope detection
Future Improvements: Upgrade to an instrumentation amplifier such as AD620
Add a notch filter for power line interference
Implement multi-stage amplification with adjustable gain
Add digital signal processing for better control
Add wireless data transmission using Bluetooth or WiFi
Portfolio Value: Shows a complete bio-signal to actuation pipeline
Demonstrates real-world EMG control with a custom PCB
Acts as a foundation for prosthetics, robotics, and human-machine interface systems
